text.p: Grupo Modelo, Mexico's leading brewer, completed an "extraordinary year" in 1996 with significant increases in domestic and export sales volumes, the company's No. 2 executive said on Thursday.

"We still haven't consolidated all our figures, but nonetheless I can say ... our (domestic) sales volume could be around five percent more (than in 1995)," Carlos Fernandez Gonzalez, who carries the title general coordinator, told Reuters in an interview.

Fernandez Gonzalez said 1996 was an "extraordinary year" in which export sales volumes grew between 24 percent and 26 percent from the 2.89 million hectoliters sold abroad in 1995. He said domestic sales volumes grew by about five percent from 22.22 million hectoliters the previous year.

Modelo, due to announce official 1996 earnings in late Feburary, controls about 55 percent of the national beer market with 10 brands. It also has posted healthy export growth in recent years, led by its Corona brand, with 1996 exports representing 14 percent of total volume and 20 percent of its billing, Fernandez Gonzalez said.
